rubrics.justification: The response misstates key morphology: it calls the embryo a good-quality/full blastocyst and describes TE as B-grade, whereas the image/lab label 2AB indicates an early blastocyst with strong ICM and looser/scant TE. It also speculates about hatching/collapse and zona thinning without clear visual support.

It integrates most relevant factors well: age 31, BMI, FSH, male factor context, prior biochemical/failed cycles, endometrial thickness, and lifestyle, and relates these to prognosis. It misses some nuance around absent AMH and overstates semen reassurance despite male-factor diagnosis.

The overall logic is understandable, but there are inconsistencies: probability estimates shift from 40-60% to 35-50% to 30-45%, and morphology interpretation conflicts with the provided Gardner score. Conclusions are generally supported but somewhat internally unstable.

Recommendations are largely consistent with IVF practice: single embryo transfer at age 31, standard luteal support, avoidance of unproven add-ons, and consideration of uterine and sperm-factor workup after repeated failures. Minor deviation comes from confusion around Gardner staging and somewhat speculative PGT-A discussion in a young patient.

Provides practical next steps for transfer and future planning, including SET, luteal support, review of embryo cohort quality, sperm DNA fragmentation/strict morphology, and uterine evaluation if failures continue. Useful, though some suggestions remain broad rather than tightly prioritized.
